title: Integral duality and a finite extension of coefficient fields
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ use the completed coefficient sheaves $\widehat R_X$ and $\widehat S_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and their ordinary sheaves of modules. Write
$$T_{S/R}K=K\widehat\otimes_R^L S$$
for the strict-tower integral scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], identified on derived-complete inputs with ordinary derived tensor $K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}\widehat S_X$ by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. It is exact and preserves the integral bounded constructible categories of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Internal Hom means the ambient derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $\omega_{X,R}$ and $\omega_{X,S}$ are the integral dualizing objects [prop-coef-integral-dualizing], and $D_{X,R}$ and $D_{X,S}$ are the ambient integral Verdier duals [thm-coef-integral-verdier].

For $K,M\in D^b_c(X,R)$ there are canonical isomorphisms
$$
u_{L/E}:T_{S/R}\omega_{X,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,S},
\qquad
v_{K,M}:T_{S/R}R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}(K,M)
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat S_X}(T_{S/R}K,T_{S/R}M),
$$
and consequently
$$
\beta_{L/E,K}:T_{S/R}D_{X,R}K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,S}(T_{S/R}K).
$$
They commute with evaluation and with the canonical map $K\to D_{X,R}D_{X,R}K$. They are compatible with finite coefficient quotients [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], the identity extension, and composition of finite field extensions, including the tensor associators.

proof.text: The canonical definitions, u_existsUnique and its new proved reduction equation are relocated unchanged to the core module to avoid an import cycle with the three partial comparison lemmas. Their proof is recorded in def-sf-integral-finite-extension-core.

Choose source and target signed tensor presentations with all quotient presentations by signedCalculus, together with its first-variable evaluation naturality for the source, target and every finite target presentation. The target naturality supplies the hypothesis of the proved evaluation_transport helper. Apply comparison_invertibility for triangulation and invertibility of u,v, reductionPairing (with both swap and all evaluation naturalities) for the double-dual and two Hom reduction squares, and comparison_cocycles (with the naturality of a, b and of the given c) for the identity/composition assertions.

Use sfIntegralScalarExtension_constructible on each input. Beta is a composite of v with the functorial image of the isomorphism u, hence is invertible. The proved evaluation_transport identity combines first-variable evaluation naturality with the target adjunction counit naturality; apply it to completion.inv, homMap and completion.hom. The homMap evaluation cancels by homEquiv.symm_apply_apply, giving the v evaluation clause. Postcompose by u using counit naturality to get beta evaluation. Finally u_reduction is the chosen witness specification. Assemble all conjuncts and coefficient cocycles without any additional hole.

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs 1-7: Lean assembly from three proper partial comparison statements, with constructibility, beta invertibility, evaluation and u reduction proved in the assembly.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\Ql$, put
$R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$, and write
$T_{S/R}K=\mathcal O_{L,X}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}K$. This exact functor preserves
the integral bounded constructible categories. There are canonical
isomorphisms

$$
u_{L/E}:T_{S/R}\omega_{X,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,S},
\qquad
v_{K,M}:T_{S/R}R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_S(T_{S/R}K,T_{S/R}M),
$$

and consequently

$$
\beta_{L/E,K}:T_{S/R}D_{X,R}K
\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,S}(T_{S/R}K)
\qquad(K,M\in D^b_c(X,R)).
$$

They commute with evaluation and with the canonical map
$K\to D_{X,R}D_{X,R}K$. They are compatible with finite
coefficient quotients, the identity extension, and composition of
finite field extensions, including the tensor associators.

proof.text:
The $R$-module $S$ is finite free, so $\mathcal O_{L,X}=S\otimes_R\mathcal O_{E,X}$
is a finite free $\mathcal O_{E,X}$-module
([sk-prop-sfb-finite-extension-compatibility]); its tensor functor is
exact and commutes with derived inverse limits. In particular
$T_{S/R}$ preserves derived completeness [def-pe-derived-complete], and no completion is needed. If $e$
is the ramification index, the ideals
$\pi_E^nS=\pi_L^{en}S$ are a cofinal system of powers of
the maximal ideal of $S$. The reductions of $T_{S/R}K$ along
this system are

$$
(S/\pi_E^nS)\otimes_{R/\pi_E^n}^LK_n,
\qquad K_n=K\otimes_R^L R/\pi_E^n.
$$

They are constructible and have a uniform Tor interval, since
[lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] supplies that interval for
$K_n$ and finite free extension preserves it. The normalized
tower reconstruction of [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]
therefore gives an object of $D^b_c(X,S)$. The intervening
$\pi_L$-reductions are recovered by derived tensor from
any larger cofinal level, so they have the same Tor bound.

By [prop-coef-integral-dualizing], the reductions of the
integral dualizing objects are the finite dualizing objects.
At the cofinal levels [lem-coef-finite-free-extension] gives
the specified maps

$$
(S/\pi_E^nS)\otimes_{R/\pi_E^n}^L\omega_{X,R/\pi_E^n}
\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,S/\pi_E^nS}.
$$

Their quotient compatibility makes them a map of normalized
derived towers. Taking the derived limit, and using the
finite-free tensor comparison above, gives
$u_{L/E}$, including its naturality and compatibility with the
dualizing counit. This argument uses coherent maps of towers,
not just isomorphism classes of their terms.

The map $v_{K,M}$ is the transpose of scalar-extended
evaluation. To prove it is an isomorphism, forget the
$S$-action. Extension–restriction adjunction identifies its
target with
$R\mathcal Hom_R(K,S\otimes_RM)$. Locally choose a finite
free $R$-basis of $S$. Both this object and the source
identify with the corresponding finite sum of
$R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)$, and $v_{K,M}$ becomes the identity
comparison of these sums. Forgetting coefficients is conservative,
so the comparison is an isomorphism. This reasoning uses finite
freeness of the coefficient extension, with no perfectness
assumption on $K$ on the whole space. All these internal Hom
objects are integral bounded constructible objects by
[cor-coef-integral-internal-hom].

Compose $v_{K,\omega_{X,R}}$ with internal Hom into
$u_{L/E}$ to obtain $\beta_{L/E,K}$. It identifies the
ambient integral duals of [thm-coef-integral-verdier].
Evaluation compatibility follows from the definition by
transposition. Transposing evaluation once more gives compatibility
with the double-dual map. For nested rings $R\subset S\subset U$,
the associator being used is

$$
U\otimes_S^L(S\otimes_R^LK)\xrightarrow{\sim}U\otimes_R^LK.
$$

For $u$, the unit and composition equations are the equations
of the finite comparisons, transported through derived inverse
limit. For $v$, both composites transpose to the
same evaluation after this associator; hence they are equal.
The same is true for $\beta$. These arguments also prove
compatibility with finite quotients and involve no chosen basis
in the definition of any comparison.
